spec.description: What one station reported over a span of time, newest first. Airport stations report about every twenty minutes, and more often when the weather changes, so a day is a few hundred observations.

station_id.description: Station identifier, such as `KSEA`. `stations.list_stations` returns it as `stationIdentifier`.

start.description: Start of the span, inclusive. The service keeps about a week of observations; a start older than that returns nothing rather than failing.

limit.description: Observations per response. Range [1, 500]; the service caps a response at 500 whether or not this is sent, so 500 is also the default.

response.title: ObservationCollection
response.description: The observations in the span, as a GeoJSON feature collection, newest first.

pagination.title: ObservationPagination
pagination.description: Where the next page is, as a whole URL. The declared walk moves the time window instead and never reads this.

next.description: URL of the next page. Absent on the last one.

notes: Both bounds are inclusive, so the step is one second: a window whose `end` equalled the previous window's `start` would re-read the observation on the boundary.

The service also pages this endpoint by cursor, in a `pagination.next` URL. The time window is the walk a caller actually means here -- "what did this station report yesterday" -- and it is the one that can be declared, since the cursor arrives inside a URL rather than on its own.

`limit` declares `default: 500` because that is what the service does, not because it documents it: a six-day span of KSEA observations comes back as exactly 500 rows with `limit` sent and with it omitted. The declared default is what arms the walk's truncation guard -- without it a caller asking for a week silently gets the newest 500 observations and no indication that the rest were withheld.
